Public Facilities
The proposed "Operation Clean-Up" and the improvements to the George Mayne School park will not involve geologic impacts.
Campus CNRA:
Housing Rehabilitation
Loans will be made available for housing rehabilitations in this area. It is an area of multi-story dwelling and high liquefaction potential, though it is beyond the boundary of the Silver Creek Fault trace zone, structural improvements of sub-standard units in the Campus CNRA will have a positive impact.
Capital Improvements
None planned; no impact.
Public Facilities
Funds are provided for rehabilitation of the existing building areas being used for John XXIII Senior Center.
Gardner CNRA:
Housing Rehabilitation
Theloans and grants available to an estimated 103 houses in this neighborhood should be used in part to improve the seismic safety of these structures. The seismic response of the alluvial materials underlying this and other older neighborhoods have a long period for major earthquakes (Cooper-Clark Assoc., 1974) and should not be sympathetic with the response of single family dwellings. Older structures in this and other areas, however, could experience more damage due to a lack of basic seismic structural elements. While it is not always economically feasible to implement structural modifications to existing buildings, it should be possible in the case of wood-frame dwellings. The most important requirement would be to provide bracing or anchorage to the foundation, plus improving the stability of chimneys, tile roofs, water heaters and masonary veneers.
The extent that CDBG loans and grants are used to identify and rectify structural deficiencies, the impact will be positive. In cases where necessary rehabilitation is not possible, demolition of seismically unsafe dwellings and relocation of residents to new areas or to a new structure on the same site, will have a positive impact.
